reviews.comment: Watch the videos, utilize the practice exams (very similar to exams) and study the reaction/mechanism sheets. I only studied with these materials, and I got A's on all of the exams. Lecture is required though it's just a reiteration of what's on the provided videos. A lot of work, but the way he structures and curves the course makes it doable.

Nice man with engaging lectures. Very helpful during office hours and also conducts review sessions once a week. His graders are pretty quick; we got all exam scores within 2 days. No extra credit, but curved an A to 84.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of HW but Aktiv goes fast. The class is very test-heavy, however, know how to do the sample/practice exams and you will do fine. The cutoff for an A was 84. He holds office hours every weekday and a review on Monday nights. SI also helped a lot. Very caring and even cracks a couple of jokes. I recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for 227, and now 228. Hands down my favorite professor so far. His exams were fair, and he is a very good lecturer, actually promotes learning of the concepts. If he teaches ochem 3 I'd take him.

DO NOT TAKE HIM TAKE ANYONE ELSE. Old guy, talks quietly, accent is hard to understand. A lot of Aktiv homework weekly. Exams are nothing like homework. All free response exams, very hard, and no partial credit. Grades exams harshly. No extra credit. Attendance is mandatory but the "easy" points do not make a difference on overall course grade.

Santander's class is quite difficult. Tests were weighted heavily and many dropped. He lowered the grade criteria by 14% because so many of his students were failing. He does not give the entire period for exams and begins teaching in the last half hour, so you need to try and focus while he teacher. Chemistry puzzles are the absolute worst.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Santander is a phenomenal professor. Take this class knowing O Chem itself is just difficult material to digest. The supplemental video lectures are a godsend and the homework is relatively light but helpful. He gives so much material to prepare for exams and the SI sessions make an A very attainable.
Soo bad at lecturing, made me want to  myself after every lecture. Not useful had to reach myself the course

His exams are very doable, especially if you attend lecture and SI. The exams are pretty similar to the practice questions. He also curves the grades at the end of the semester, so getting an A or B is attainable as long as you put in effort with the practice.

Dr. Santander may not be the easiest professor you can take but he does lower his cutoffs depending on how everyone is doing. His exams can be challenging, and be expected to read and stay on top of the materials before going to class but I think that's just the nature of the material. He does make funny jokes that makes ochem more tolerable.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He was a pretty good professor considering the other ochem profs, but not compared to other profs in general. reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this prof, he was incredibly considerate of students time and energy. He offered tons of review sessions and had lots of extra study material. He makes it incredibly easy to be successful. Go to class, the review sessions, and office hours and use the review sheets/practice questions and you'll be set! All in all, my favorite prof at TAMU!

Profesor Santander was a good professor for ochem 2! The fist time I took it I q dropped it but this time I almost made an A, his exams are similar to the practice but he does change things, he was very nice and understanding if you go talk to him. He has high expectations and 95% grade are exams, there was a curve at the end! Recommend!!

Ochem 2 is a hard class but I don't feel like this professor made it more digestable in any way. I found that the lectures didn't really cover reactions in an intentional way to teach important material. He is pretty nice and a fair grader, however I had to use other resources to prepare for tests. Not the best but could be worse I guess

CHEM 228 for Spring Semester. Prof Santander utilizes a reversed classroom. There are 5 exams including the final worth 96.15% of your final grade and the homework makes up the remainder. Videos are provided that cover the PowerPoint slides. Sample questions and practice exams are provided to prepare for each exam. Study the reactions! Does curve.

CHEM 227 for Fall Semester. Prof Santander utilizes a reversed classroom. There are 5 exams including the final worth 96.15% of your final grade and the homework makes up the remainder. Videos are provided that cover the PowerPoint slides. Sample questions and practice exams are provided to prepare for each exam. Study the reactions! Does curve.

Personally, I had to read the textbook to pass the class. I did well in OCHEM 1 but switched profs for OCHEM 2. His lectures are just reading the powerpoint so you're better off just reading each chapter (TRUST ME). I went from a 60 average to 90 average after I made the switch. You cannot rely on lectures for this class! (Also, I didn't use A+)

Santander runs flipped classroom style, his youtube vids are more helpful than his lectures for learning material. Lots of OWL homework. I do think his grading was merciful on exams, more so than other ochem professors (I had Sczepanski for ochem 1 and he gave much less partial credit).Easier ochem professor, but others put more effort into lecture

Very nice guy and wants students to do good in his class, but I wish the grade wasn't based only on exams. I didn't do good in his class, but only have myself to blame since some students do. Lectures are counterproductive because he repeats what he says in his videos. HW is worth little points. Overall, not a bad professor, just not my style.

Dr. Santander is a very sweet person, but the class is unspeakable difficult. His lectures are very useless and you have to learn the material yourself through his videos and the textbook. Your grade depends on all exams and 5% homework which takes hours to do and is very hard/useless too. No extra credit/grace and half the class drops by midterms.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he sucks, is borderline hostile during office hours and lectures are useless, is not clear about test content and the only reason for my success is my burning hate and spite for him
don't do it
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Santander for both Chem 227 and 228. Got a solid B in 227 and an A in 228. Ochem is hard, but Santander makes it doable. He provides reaction sheets and the mechanisms which are very useful. Flipped classroom model may not work for some, and the practice exams are very close to the real thing. He does not curve much, but an A is possible.

Uses the flipped classroom style. It was very annoying to sign up for a class at a certain time expecting to learn ochem at that time only to have the prof refuse to teach during his allotted time. The class material isn't that hard, I taught myself using the textbook. Exams are mostly like his practice exams. Practicing the hw helps too.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No extra credit, homework worth only 10% the rest is based on exams. Don't take him if you didn't have him for 227 otherwise you'll only be confused because he doesn't explain thoroughly. Has "flipped" classroom, so you have to watch his youtube lectures before class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First exams are easy but it gets harder each time so start off strong! He does favor smarter students and moves really fast. Dont go to class unprepared, read textbook before. first few exams are basically identical to mock exams BUT this is not true always. He does add stuff that we do not see on mock exam sometimes. Go to SI  before an exams!

If you are prepared to teach yourself ochem, then go ahead and sign up. He offers practice exams but I wish we had been graded on other things besides exams. He's a really nice guy, but teaches like we all have phd's in ochem. Lectures are extremely unhelpful and, in my opinion, counterproductive. Would not put myself through this torture again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His accent makes it very hard to understand what he's teaching. I ended up dropping out because I had a D in the class and would've ended up with a C. Don't be scared! Everyone just wants an easy professor to not have to put in the effort. The exams are all free response, very similar to the mock. Read the book, do the practice problems at the end of the chapters, and the extra handouts he posts!! Just put in the work and you'll be absolutely fine! We did move faster than any other class though.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take with this professor! One of the worst OCHEM professors at TAMU. Nice person but hard to understand and does not teach you anything in class. He's tenured so no matter what he does, he'll never get fired. He is a great person but a horrible prof. OTHER PROFS ARE REASONABLE HE IS EXTREMELY HARD

For the love of everything please DO NOT take this professor. Dr. Santander is one of the best professors to take for CHEM227! His tests are very similar to the practice and sample exams he gives. In addition, he makes himself accessible throughout the week for questions and help.

Loved Dr. Santander. Lots of office hours so very easy to ask questions. Emails back quickly and even has a review session every week. He gives out a very helpful practice exam and the owl homework is a good study for the tests. Very nice guy and cares about making sure his students understand.

Santander is the best prof at A&M. I took him for both ochem's and he has been amazing during COVID. The class is test heavy in grading but for summer he gave more points to OWL. Dr. Santandar is an awesome professor! He truly does try to make everyone pass the class, and he curves! He will drop the highest grades and make a true curve, he wants everyone to make a good grade! He brings you coughdrops and inspirational quotes to the test. Highly recommend him!!

Santander exams are extremely hard and long. He does not give partial credit and does not care for his students. He doesn't care if your failing and need help. Santander is genuinely excited to teach, and he gives your plenty of resources to succeed. His tests are hard because he truly tests your understanding of the material, but he's a great professor.

His lectures can be confusing sometimes but going to the SI really helped. He puts out practice exams for each exam that are really helpful and give you an idea of whats on the test. taking him again for 228

Santander was an excellent professor. He cared for his students and wanted us to really learn the material. His tests were very fair. I learned a lot in his class. on of the best profs at a&m!! cares so much about us doing well and gives you everything you need to be successful. practice tests are similar to real test so you always know what to expect. If you put in the work and pay attention in class an A is more than possible. seriously amazing take him

reviews.comment: Santander is a great prof. The material is very difficult but he is well educated on the subject and will try and walk you through it as best as he can. He offers help sessions and office hours, and gives you a practice test before each exam. Will take him again for 228!
Incredibly helpful and truly cares about the success of his students. The course is difficult but he definitely makes it bearable. I would take him again if I could!

Dr. Santander is probably my favorite professor at A&M. I had him for both 227/228 and learned so much in his class. He expects students to perform their best, and will reward you in the end if you put in the effort. An A will not come easy, he makes you work for it. He spends so much time outside of the classroom helping students. Great professor!

Dr. Santander is a great professor for ochem. He will teach you if you let him. Ochem is a very tough subject in general, but he wants you to do well and will help you when you need it. Do everything you can to keep up to date in this class because you can fall behind really easily, and almost everything builds on top of itself.

Very helpful teacher and in general the lectures are useful. Unfortunately his tests are very hard and this was probably the hardest course I have taken. Would definatley recommend going to all SI Sessions.

Dr. Santandar is a great teacher. Go to his office hours. He is super helpful and learns the names of his students. His sample tests are extremely similar to his tests. I recommend reading, going to class for clarification, then attending office hours for OWLS help. He gives you tons of extra practice and a packet with all your mechanisms.

Dr. Santander is one of the best profs I had. Coming into ochem, I wasn't strong in general chemistry. I went to him at the beginning of the semester and he took time to explain topics from gen chem to me. He is very accessible as he has tons of office hours. His tests are very fair & his practice tests are a good representation of the actual test
He's super sweet and helpful. Office hours everyday are amazing!! Lectures are from the book, but he will draw stuff on the blackboard and explain things, which is helpful.

Professor Santander is a great professor and just a great guy. His lectures weren't always the most helpful, but he is very knowledgeable and, with work, you can succeed in his class. Gives very helpful handouts for reactions and puts in a ton of work for his students. Practice exams are almost identical to exams given. Overall an excellent prof!

At the beginning of the semester, he told us he was from chill, and he wasn't kidding. This guy is the chillest prof I've ever had, like so chill. I don't know where "chill" means, but he's even gonna give some of us chocolate from chill.

Ochem is hard, but his lectures are very informative and clear. Make it easy on yourself and go to class and review sessions because he is really good at explaining things and he will also help you in office hours. Awesome teacher.

One of the worst professors I have taken. He made me very upset when I did go to talk to him and never helped or answered questions clearly. He doesn't care whether or not you learn or even pass the class and his accent is hard to understand. If you can get ANY other professor- do!

As I've heard from other students, he is a much better o chem 1 prof, but for o chem 2 he seems very scatterbrained. He definitely knows what he's talking about but doesn't seem to be able to stick to one topic at a time. He goes through the material very quickly and offers help one on one, but every time i left feeling more discouraged.

Naturally O-Chem is not easy.  Santander knows his material and is very helpful.  He wants his students to pass, but if you fail to attend class and fail to study, what would you expect but a poor grade?  Santander is super cute and very enjoyable to pay attention to, which makes it easy to attend classes.  The rest is up to you.

Read that he was pretty easy, so I took him. He would post practice tests, but the real tests were nothing like them and he likes to post tricky questions on the test...the class average for most of the tests are around a 65. The people i talked to who took him for ochemI and thought he was easy then now think that he is way harder in o chemII.

After reading some of the reviews I thought he would be a nice guy. If you do not understand general chemistry do not take him. If you are weak in general chemistry he will look down on you and not take the time to try to help you. He will look at you like you are a lost cause. Brush up on gen chem and elctronegativity before entering that class.

Great prof, really cares about his students. Good sense of humor, very kind & personable. Posted practice tests are almost identical to exams except for actual numbers. Very accessible before/after class, during posted office hours, & for drop-ins outside of ofc hours. Will spend as long as you need explaining a topic. One of my fave profs ever.

He seems to be one of the nicest organic chemistry professors out there.  If you're looking for a prof who lays out everything in a straightforward manner, choose Santander.  He puts up practice exams similar to the real thing.  He's never too heavy on OWL homework and is highly helpful.
His tests are very straight forward and he is super nice. He will not try to trick you in any way on the exams.
